annotations.description: Howling Mine is a symmetrical draw effect that benefits all four opponents equally. In a 4-player game, you draw 1 extra card per turn cycle but your opponents collectively draw 3 extra cards. This is especially bad when played early (turn 3) as it accelerates opponents into their threats and answers. Meanwhile, Jotun Grunt is a 4/4 for 2 mana that applies pressure and can manage graveyards. Additionally, Gem3F Stoic already has a Baleful Strix on board that benefits from extra cards, and DSV3 Spike has Jet Medallion to cast cheaper spells drawn off the Mine.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Howling Mine, giving all opponents extra draws
annotations.betterLine: Cast Jotun Grunt as a 4/4 body for 2 mana to apply early pressure and control graveyards, rather than giving opponents card advantage with Howling Mine

annotations.description: Casting Skirsdag High Priest first instead of Mind Stone. While both could potentially be cast this turn (total 3 mana needed, 4 available), Mind Stone should be the priority to ensure mana ramp toward Drana on turn 4. Skirsdag High Priest is nearly useless without other creatures and morbid, making it a very low-impact play on its own. If for some reason only one spell gets cast, Mind Stone is clearly better.

annotations.description: DSV3 Spike has 5 lands (including Jet Medallion for cost reduction) and Mind Stone in hand, but chose to pass without playing anything. Mind Stone costs 2 mana and would provide ramp for the expensive cards in hand (Drana at 5 mana, Evernight Shade at 4 mana, Skeletal Scrying). With only 4 lands producing mana plus Jet Medallion, deploying Mind Stone accelerates toward casting Drana or Syr Konrad-level threats a turn earlier. Swiftfoot Boots (also 2 mana) could also be deployed to protect a future Drana. There's no reason to hold mana open with no instants worth casting at this point in the game (Skeletal Scrying with X=0 is useless, and Black Sun's Zenith for X=0 or X=1 isn't needed yet).

annotations.description: Gem3F Stoic has Krosan Grip in hand and MiMo Vorthos has Howling Mine on the battlefield, which benefits all opponents equally. Destroying Howling Mine with Krosan Grip (which has split second, so it can't be responded to) would deny card advantage to all three opponents while Stoic already has a strong hand with Damnation, Cryptic Command, Mystical Teachings, and Miscalculation. Instead, they chose to cast Sylvan Library, which is a strong card but could have been played next turn after removing Howling Mine. However, Sylvan Library is excellent and playing it early maximizes its value over time, and Howling Mine does also give Stoic extra draws. The decision is defensible but debatable - Howling Mine helping three opponents vs. one player is generally bad for the table, and Stoic already has a full hand.

annotations.description: Goblin Cadets is a 2/1 for R with the significant downside that whenever it blocks or becomes blocked, an opponent gains control of it. In a multiplayer game, this creature is almost always a liability - it can't attack profitably into any board with blockers without giving itself away, and it can't block without the same problem. Meanwhile, Soul Snare (W enchantment that can exile an attacking creature) provides defensive value, and Windborn Muse (3W flying 2/3 that taxes attackers) would be castable next turn and provides much better board presence. Crescendo of War (3W) is also available and could be impactful. Playing a creature that will likely be given away to an opponent seems low-value compared to deploying Soul Snare for 1 mana, which provides immediate defensive utility.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Soul Snare (W) instead, which provides actual defensive value without the risk of giving an opponent a creature. Soul Snare can exile an attacking creature targeting you or your planeswalker, offering real protection.

annotations.description: Ob Nixilis is at 3 loyalty and using -2 brings it to 1 loyalty, making it very vulnerable. The +2 ability would bring it to 5 loyalty (much safer) while draining 3 life from opponents (1 each from 3 opponents) and gaining 3 life. With Howling Mine giving extra draws, protecting the planeswalker for repeated value over multiple turns could be more impactful than a single 5/5 demon token that costs 2 life. However, a 5/5 flyer is a significant threat in multiplayer, and it enables Skirsdag High Priest's morbid-related synergies and provides a sacrifice target for Infernal Offering in hand. The decision is defensible but the loyalty risk is real.
